content.rendered:
He died way too young at the age of 21, but he left us with a string of rockabilly classics that would influence generations of artists to come.

Eddie Cochran’s biggest hit was “Summertime Blues,” a song Springsteen covered as far back as the Darkness Tour. But that’s not the only song of Cochran’s that Bruce covered.

On the evening of July 23, 1982, Bruce joined rockabilly band Stray Cats on guitar at The Fast Lane for a one-time-only cover of Cochran’s “Twenty Flight Rock.”

Cochran’s original performance of “Twenty Flight Rock” debuted in the 1956 movie The Girl Can’t Help It. Eddie was only eighteen at the time.

Cochran released “Twenty Flight Rock” as a single the following year, but it never became a hit.

That didn’t stop it from being an important, influential song, however:

On July 6, 1957, a fifteen-year-old Liverpool musician chose “Twenty Flight Rock” as his first song for his audition for a local band called The Quarrymen–and he played it so well that the young Paul McCartney was asked to join The Quarrymen by its leader, one John Lennon.

Twenty Flight Rock
First performed: July 23, 1982 (Asbury Park, NJ)
Last performed: July 23, 1982 (Asbury Park, NJ)

© April 13, 2020

excerpt.rendered: One time only: Bruce teams up with Stray Cats at The Fast Lane on Eddie Cochran’s rockabilly classic.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Summertime Blues
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: With can't-catch-a-break lyrics belied by an infectious and instantly recognizable riff, "Summertime Blues" was tailor-made for a Springsteen set list. Watch some of Bruce's great performances of it inside.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Long Tall Sally
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Lots of times with lots of people: "Long Tall Sally" is tried and true when Bruce joins fellow musicians for an impromptu jam. Check out some of his best performances inside.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Brand New Cadillac
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: One time only: Bruce and The Wallflowers cover Vince Taylor's 1959 rockabilly classic, "Brand New Cadillac."

jetpack-related-posts.title: Blue Suede Shoes
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: One time only (and *almost* another): Bruce joins John Eddie on Carl Perkins' breakthrough rockabilly hit.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Do You Want to Dance
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: One time only: Listen to Bruce Springsteen join Rhode Island rockers Beaver Brown in a joyful cover of Bobby Freeman’s “Do You Want to Dance” in a surprise appearance in the summer of 1982.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Rock Baby, Rock It
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: One time only: Bruce Springsteen joins Stone Pony house band Cats on a Smooth Surface to cover a lost rockabilly classic.
